title: Construct in memory you already have
description:
`new` does two jobs: it gets memory, and it constructs an object there. They can be separated. This is how `std::optional` and `std::vector` hold space for an object that does not exist yet.

Write `template <typename T> class Slot`: storage for one `T` that may or may not currently hold an object.

- The storage is a raw buffer inside the slot, correctly sized and aligned: `alignas(T) std::byte m_storage[sizeof(T)];` No heap allocation at all.
- `template <typename... Args> T& emplace(Args&&... args)`: if an object is already there, destroy it first; then construct a new `T` in the buffer with `std::construct_at` and return it.
- `void reset()`: destroys the object if there is one (`std::destroy_at`).
- `bool hasValue() const`, and `T& get()` (only called when there is a value).
- The destructor calls `reset()`.
- Not copyable.
lessonTitle: Custom Memory: Placement new, Allocators and PMR
